I1.quote: The hydrogenation of the MWNTs was measured by thermogravimetric analysis. Here ultrahigh pure hydrogen gas was used. ... The 10s_MWNTs had the highest hydrogen-storage capacity (0.87 wt%)

I2.quote: The as-received MWNTs were purchased from Shenzhen Nanotech Port Co., Ltd, China. These MWNTs have a purity of >95 % and were synthesized by chemical-vapor deposition.

I3.quote: Searched the 'Hydrogenation conditions' section, the 'Hydrogenation' results, Fig. 5 (bar chart, no axis; caption 'Hydrogen-adsorption capacities of MWNTs'), the abstract and the conclusion for a numerical temperature of any H2 uptake value. Not found: the pressure is stated (3 MPa) but the temperature only in words, 'to a maximum pressure of 3 MPa at room temperature' and 'at room temperature' in the abstract. Under the schema (data dictionary, temperature_unstated), 'room temperature' is a condition stated only in words, not a number, and is not imputed. The only numerical temperature, 22 °C, belongs to the neutron diffraction under 2 MPa D2, which gives no uptake value.

I4.quote: According to the BET analysis, there was no discernible increase in specific surface area of MWNTs after microwave treatment. For s_MWNTs with smaller diameters, the specific areas were 128 ± 0.6 and 136 ± 0.4 m2/g
I4.location: main, p. 3 (journal p. 1310), Results and discussion, 'Characterization of the as-received and the irradiated MWNTs'

I5.quote: Microwave irradiation is a simple yet effective way of altering the properties of multiwalled carbon nanotubes (MWNTs).

notes: Original research article (J Mater Sci 2016), not retracted per record.json and the PDF; no statement that the uptake values were published before (only the procedure is referred to 'our previous paper [8]'). Uptake is gravimetric (TGA under continuous H2 purge to 3 MPa, tangent-mass and He-reference buoyancy correction), on commercial CVD MWNTs; BET areas reported for s_MWNTs and l_MWNTs before and after microwave treatment. The sole failing criterion is I3, and it rests on one judgment: the uptake temperature is given only as 'room temperature'. I applied the schema's rule that a temperature stated only in words is unstated and not imputed. If an adjudicator reads 'room temperature' as a stated temperature for I3, all of I1 to I5 are met, no other code applies, and the paper is eligible.
